question.worked_solution:
We start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 & 5 \\ 4 & 6 & -10 \\ 6 & 9 & -15\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 6 & 9 & -15\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to basis vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the reduced matrix has $1$ pivot column (or alternatively, it has exactly $1$ non-zero row). 

Therefore, 
$\text{dim}(\text{Span}\{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4 \\ -6\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 6 \\ 9\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ -15\end{aligned}]\})=1.$
